note: Resolves the Disease Master's 'Related Markers/Tests' column against the parameter dictionary. That column is free prose, so three things have to be handled before coverage can be measured honestly: umbrella terms that name a panel rather than a parameter, prose fragments that are not markers at all, and markers for which no assay exists in the dictionary. tools/coverage.py uses this file; anything not covered here and not resolvable by alias is reported as a genuine gap.
not_markers: included here as part of the same bone-metabolism marker set)
not_markers_note: Prose fragments left behind when the free-text marker list is split on commas, plus the allergen examples listed inside 'Specific IgE panel for common food allergens (peanut, tree nuts, milk, ...)'. The head term of each of those phrases does resolve; these are the tail. They are excluded from the coverage denominator because they are not markers.

no_assay_available.reason: No tryptase assay in the NG catalogue. The Disease Master itself notes it is only informative if drawn during or shortly after the reaction.
No anti-ganglioside assay in the catalogue. The Disease Master qualifies this marker with 'where available'; the CSF protein arm of the same row is implemented and is what the cluster fires on.
No TB-specific assay (IGRA, AFB smear, GeneXpert) in the catalogue. Adding one would make Tuberculosis directly mappable.

reported_only_parameters.reason: Basophilia is rare and non-specific; its main association is with myeloproliferative disease, which the Disease Master does not carry a row for. Extracted, graded and shown, but not used to drive any cluster.
Clinically useful mainly for stone type and renal tubular acidosis, neither of which is a Disease Master row. Extracted and shown.
Carries no risk meaning on its own. Recorded and shown alongside Rh factor, which is the component with a Disease Master mapping.

Added so the urine dipstick 'Bilirubin' resolves to its own parameter instead of colliding with SERUM Total Bilirubin, which it was overwriting. No Disease Master row names urine bilirubin as a marker, so it is extracted and shown but drives no cluster.
